# Fire and Bushfire {#sec-fire}

::: {.chapter-goal}
#### In this chapter
You will answer the three questions every fire agency and insurer asks after a large fire: how dry was the fuel, how did the fire spread, and how badly did it burn. Then you will check the answer against a second, independent product.
:::

## Three questions, three datasets

| Question | Data | What it measures |
|---|---|---|
| How dry was the fuel? | MODIS NDMI, monthly | water in the canopy, as an anomaly from normal |
| How did the fire spread? | MODIS burned area (MCD64A1) and FIRMS active fire | the date each place burned; daily fire detections |
| How badly did it burn? | Sentinel-2 dNBR | the drop in the normalised burn ratio, before to after |

These are the building blocks of the author's bushfire monitors for New South Wales. Here they are applied to one of the largest fires of the 2019–20 Black Summer, in the Wollemi and Blue Mountains.

::: {.callout-important}
## Scientific integrity: severity classes are borrowed, and burned area has two answers
The dNBR classes come from Key and Benson's field protocol for North American forest. They have not been calibrated for eucalypt forest, so read "high severity" as "large change in NBR", not as a measured effect on trees. Burned area also depends on the sensor. The 20 m Sentinel-2 map and the 500 m MODIS product agree on about 626,000 ha, but the two disagree on another 377,000 ha. Report the overlap, not just one number.
:::

## From fire to peat and back

In Indonesia the same three questions apply to peat fires, with one difference: most of the carbon burns below the surface, where no optical sensor sees it. Chapter 37 (peatland) returns to that.

## Exercises {.unnumbered}

1. Move the "pre" window to the same months two years earlier. How much of the dNBR signal is drought, not fire?
2. Plot FIRMS detections against the NDMI anomaly month by month. Did the fire season start when the canopy dried?
3. Find where Sentinel-2 says burned and MODIS does not. Are those small patches, edges, or real disagreements?
